concept: Foundation of the Indian National Congress
question: Who among the following was the first woman President of the Indian National Congress?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Annie Besant**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Annie Besant** became the first woman President of the Indian National Congress in **1917**.
 
• She played a significant role in the **Home Rule Movement**, advocating self-governance for India.
 
• Annie Besant was an Irish-born British socialist, theosophist, and supporter of Indian independence.
 
• Her presidency marked a pivotal moment in the Indian freedom struggle, symbolizing the growing participation of women in politics.
 
• She was also a prolific writer and speaker, contributing to the intellectual and social awakening in India during the early 20th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian National Congress (INC)**

 
 
• Founded in **1885**, the INC played a significant role in India's struggle for independence.
 
• Early leaders of the INC included A.O. Hume, Dadabhai Naoroji, and W.C. Bonnerjee.
 
• The INC initially aimed at moderate reforms but later shifted toward demanding complete independence.
 
 
 
• **Home Rule Movement**
 
 
• Initiated by Annie Besant and Bal Gangadhar Tilak in **1916**.
 
• It sought self-governance and autonomy within the British Empire.
 
• The movement helped galvanize Indian nationalist sentiment during World War I.
 
 
 
• **Role of Women in Freedom Struggle**
 
 
• Women like Sarojini Naidu, Aruna Asaf Ali, and Kasturba Gandhi played crucial roles in India's independence movement.
 
• The participation of women in the INC and other movements marked the beginning of broader gender inclusion in Indian politics.
 
 
 
• **Annie Besant's Legacy**
 
 
• She founded the **Theosophical Society** and worked on educational reforms in India.
 
• Her efforts contributed to the establishment of the Banaras Hindu University (BHU).
 
• She was deeply involved in advocating for Indian culture and philosophy on global platforms.
